ashley: Bringing up cassini13b (13B) quantized to int4 for canary. Seeing intermittent OOMs on 2/8 GPUs during high-concurrency microbatches. Root log attached below, but pattern looks like fragmentation + large max_new_tokens requests. Anyone seen this with similar weight layouts?

sam: Can you paste the error / stack? Also what batch/window settings did you use for the canary?

ashley: Error snippet:
```
2024-04-02T15:03:21Z kernel: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
inference_service: evicting KV cache: slot_count=32768 used=31240 free=2028
prefetch: queued 24 requests, burst=8, batch_window_ms=12
max_new_tokens=1024 received from route default-model
```
We used batch_window_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=4096, adaptive_window: off, prefetch=enabled (default heur). Canary traffic mixed: long chat sessions + streaming.

denise: That max_new_tokens=1024 is suspicious with int4 on 13B. Memory per token is lower but fragmentation can blow up under continuous allocation/deallocation. Two quick ideas:
- reduce default max_new_tokens to 512 for canary (route config)
- apply a small slot_reserve for prefetched KV (e.g., reserve 5% of slots) to avoid a flurry of evictions

yuri: We saw similar on another model — int4 + streaming + long tail prompts = periodic OOMs. Our mitigations: slowstart for new sessions and a soft cap on max_new_tokens per-session. Also increased eviction threshold to keep more cold KV around instead of thrashing.

ashley: Good call. Quick repro plan I'm going to run:
- spin canary with max_new_tokens=512 and batch_window_ms=8
- disable prefetch for 30m to see effect (prefetch seems to amplify frag)
- enable slot_reserve=0.05 and evict_threshold=0.75

sam: Also run a small AB quality check — sometimes switching quant kernels or aggressive evicting can slightly change response latency/quality. Did we observe any qual regressions when you quantized?

ashley: On our eval harness there was a small increase in perplexity (~1.6%) on the summarization set after int4 conversion, mostly for very long outputs. Short-form completions looked fine.

denise: That matches expectation: int4 can change activation dynamics for long generations. For production I recommend a mixed-precision fallback for long outputs: keep int4 but fallback to int8 for requests > 600 tokens or when the model signals high uncertainty. We can implement via routing policy + model variant.

ops-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout (cassini13b-int4) started by @ashley at 2024-04-02T15:00:00Z. Monitor: /canaries/cassini13b-int4

yuri: Quick config snippet (for route override):
```yaml
routes:
  cassini-chat:
    model_variant: cassini13b-int4
    defaults:
      max_new_tokens: 512
      batch_window_ms: 8
      prefetch: false
      slot_reserve: 0.05
      evict_threshold: 0.75
    fallbacks:
      - cassini13b-int8 (weight: 0.1)
```
This keeps cost/perf but gives an automated fallback when int4 runs into mem pressure.

ashley: Ran the config for 45m with canary traffic (mixed sessions). Observations:
- OOM count dropped from ~12/hour -> 1/hour
- Latency p50 improved slightly (smaller batch_window), p95 stable
- Quality (eval harness) unchanged within noise for short tasks, long-output perplexity still +1.3%
- Prefetch off reduced fragmentation spikes per our allocator traces

sam: Sounds promising. Next steps:
1) Keep these defaults for staged canary for 24h
2) Instrument per-route token histogram to detect sessions requesting >512 tokens and route them to int8 fallback automatically
3) Add an eval gating check: if long-output perplexity delta > 2% on production prompts, pause canary

denise: I'll open a small follow-up PR with the route override + fallback route + a unit test that simulates a 1000-token streaming session. Also add a note to the model onboarding checklist about "frag-sensitive kernels" and default max_new_tokens.

ashley: thanks — I'll keep monitoring and post metrics. If the last OOMs are only at 1/hour we might be comfortable to widen to 60% traffic tomorrow.

yuri: FYI I left a trace link for allocator snapshots in the canary dashboard: /infra/traces/cassini13b/alloc-20240402

ashley: posted a short postmortem if things regress, but locking this thread for now. :thumbsup:
